materials.name: Creosote stick
materials.breakLog: The creosote stick splits along the grain.

note.name: Creosote wood
note.text: Creosote makes a short, light handle. It splits if you lean on it.

materials.name: Mesquite branch
materials.breakLog: The mesquite shaft cracks where the knot was.

note.name: Mesquite wood
note.text: A straight mesquite branch is long enough for a spear and tough enough to trust once.

note.name: Desert ironwood
note.text: Ironwood from the ridge is dense enough to sink. It makes the best long handle out here.

materials.name: Seat strut
materials.breakLog: The strut bends at the bolt hole.

note.name: Metal handles
note.text: A metal handle does not flex or split. You feel the hit land through it.

materials.name: Aluminum tube
materials.breakLog: The aluminum tube kinks in the middle.

note.name: Aluminum tubing
note.text: Aluminum tube from the wreck is long, light, and stiff. It dents before it breaks.

materials.name: Panel strip
materials.breakLog: The plastic strip snaps with a sound like a bone.

note.name: Plastic handles
note.text: Cabin plastic will do for a grip, but it bends at the wrong time and softens near a flame.

materials.name: Plastic pipe
materials.breakLog: The pipe folds where you were gripping it.

note.name: Plastic pipe
note.text: Plastic pipe is long but it bows. A spear on it thrusts a little to the side of where you aim.

materials.name: Glass shard
materials.breakLog: The glass edge shatters against the rock. You are holding a stick.

note.name: Glass edges
note.text: Glass takes an edge and loses it the first time it hits bone.

materials.name: Sheet-metal shard
materials.breakLog: The metal blade folds over at the tip.

note.name: Sheet-metal blades
note.text: Fuselage skin ground on a rock is not sharp for long, but it does not shatter.

materials.name: Knapped stone flake
materials.breakLog: The stone flake snaps off at the lashing.

note.name: Knapping chert
note.text: Chert from the ridge breaks into flakes sharper than steel. It takes an hour of patient strikes and a cut thumb.

materials.name: Heavy stone
materials.breakLog: The stone slips its lashing and rolls away.

note.name: Stone heads
note.text: A fist-sized stone lashed to a handle hits harder than your arm alone. Lash it tight or it leaves.

materials.name: Metal fitting
materials.breakLog: The fitting tears loose from the handle.

note.name: Metal heads
note.text: A seat-rail fitting is heavier for its size than any stone. Weight at the end is the whole trick.

note.name: Fuel torches
note.text: Foam and tire strip wound on a stick burn hot and fast. Two jobs of light, then ash.

note.name: Resin torches
note.text: Cloth rubbed with creosote resin burns slow and bright. It smells like rain while it does it.

note.name: Paracord
note.text: Paracord holds anything you can tie. Pull the inner strands if you need more.

materials.name: Wire
materials.breakLog: The wire unwinds on the impact.

note.name: Wire binding
note.text: Wiring from the wreck twists tight and does not burn. A torch head stays on it longer.

materials.name: Cloth strips
materials.breakLog: The cloth strips tear and the head swings free.

note.name: Cloth lashing
note.text: Strips of cabin cloth will hold a head on until the first real hit. Wet them and they shrink tighter.

note.name: Yucca fiber
note.text: Pound yucca leaves and twist the fibers. An hour of work makes a cord that will hold.

materials.name: Duct tape
materials.breakLog: The tape peels in the heat and lets go.

note.name: Duct tape
note.text: Duct tape fixes most things, except near a flame, where it melts and drips.

note.name: Sinew binding
note.text: Wet sinew wraps easily and shrinks as it dries. Nothing in the wreck binds as tight.

tools.name: Knife
tools.lengthNote: A long handle is no good for a knife.
tools.log: You seat the edge in the handle and bind it tight. It is not a factory knife. It will cut.

pattern.name: Knife pattern
pattern.text: Short handle + sharp end (glass, sheet metal, or a knapped stone flake) + binding. A factory knife is still better.

tools.name: Club
tools.log: You lash the weight to the handle. It is a club. It is also a decision about what to do when something rattles.

pattern.name: Club pattern
pattern.text: Any handle + blunt end (a heavy stone or a metal fitting) + binding.

tools.name: Spear

kindNote.plastic: Plastic flexes on a spear: −6% to kill.

tools.lengthNote: A short handle is no good for a spear. Reach is the point.
tools.log: A long shaft, an edge, a lashing pulled tight. Reach, which is most of what a spear is.

pattern.name: Spear pattern
pattern.text: Long handle (a branch or metal tubing; plastic pipe flexes) + sharp end + binding. Build it at camp.

tools.name: Torch
tools.log: You bind the head to the handle. Light for when the sun is gone.

pattern.name: Torch pattern
pattern.text: Any handle + flammable end (a fuel bundle, or cloth rubbed with creosote resin for longer) + binding. Wire keeps it burning longer; tape and plastic melt.
